verdicts.title: Partial matching width and its application to lower bounds for branching programs
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We introduce a new structural graph parameter called \emph{partial matching width}. For each (sufficiently large) integer $k \geq 1$, we introduce a class $\mathcal{G}_k$ of graphs of treewidth at most $k$ and max-degree $7$ such that for each $G \in \mathcal{G}_k$ and each (sufficiently large) $V \subseteq V(G)$, the partial matching width of $V$ is $Ω(k \log |V|)$.
  We use the above lower bound to establish a lower bound on the size of non-deterministic read-once branching programs (NROBPs).
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract addresses non-deterministic read-once BPs for CNFs of bounded treewidth via a 'partial matching width' parameter, not read-twice BPs for IP_2 or any commutator/Frobenius discrepancy measure. It shares the general 'BP lower bound' framework but does not interact with the specific conjectured ρ(P) bounds.

verdicts.title: Lower Bounds for Quantum Oblivious Transfer
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental primitive in cryptography. While perfect information theoretic security is impossible, quantum oblivious transfer protocols can limit the dishonest players' cheating. Finding the optimal security parameters in such protocols is an important open question.
